versions.notes:
- Bound the Sources destination panel and restored page scrolling when its list is hovered.
- Restricted Already imported counts and rows to the selected source scope.
- Added independent image width and height settings to Noodle settings.
- Fixed automatic timeline refresh when Marinara requires an admin secret on loopback.
- Test the agent changelog feature with a highlighted patch release. No features were added.

- Messages and notifications now share one Inbox with separate Chats and Activity
  tabs, avatar-led rows, semantic event icons, and a single navigation badge.
- Wallet now shows the active identity's unwithdrawn Creator earnings and
  spendable Fan wallet as two connected pockets, with an explicit Move to Wallet
  action and separate Spending and Earnings histories.

- Removed the visible Stories heading so the Home memory ribbon begins directly
  with its visual create and preview tiles.

- Stories on Home are now an image-first memory ribbon: compact portrait previews
  reveal each Story at a glance, while adding, unread state, and locks stay quiet.

- Removed the separators around Edit Profile and the chevron so Profile controls
  reads as one uninterrupted rail.

- Edit Profile now renders as a small tinted pill inside its full-size accessible
  rail target instead of filling the rail's height.

- Profile controls and its chevron now recede into the rail; Edit Profile alone
  keeps a restrained pink tint instead of sharing a loud solid accent block.

- Edit Profile now sits inside Profile controls immediately before the trailing
  expansion chevron, with both the label and chevron able to open the panel.

- The collapsed Profile controls rail is now a single compact 44px control:
  Edit Profile is integrated into its trailing edge instead of appearing as a
  separate button beside it.

- Creator tools are now Profile controls: a quieter unified rail that keeps Edit
  Profile inside it and reveals publishing, access, and automation only when
  expanded.

- The banner-to-profile fade now reaches the solid header exactly at the banner
  edge, removing the bright seam beneath the artwork at every avatar size.

- Creator avatars now visibly overlap about 30% of the banner artwork, while
  the identity rises into a focused dark fade that blends into the solid
  profile header.

- Profile actions now stay directly after the Creator identity and bio at every
  width, before the Creator tools and content tabs.

- Creator headers now keep the avatar high in the banner at every width, give
  mobile actions room to breathe, and keep feed controls clear and touchable on
  narrow screens.
- Header titles, focus states, and directional controls now work consistently
  for keyboard and right-to-left navigation.

- Creator identity now stays clear in the persona switcher, mobile menu selection has a visible marker, Creator cards have consistent keyboard and press feedback, and profiles show bios faithfully without pointless expansion controls.
- Stories now have a distinct Home shelf and an Add Story action that opens the Story composer directly.
- Stopped writing a warning to the log every time Slurp is opened on an Engine that cannot hold its newer tables.

- Slurp opens again. The tab crashed on load.
- The ambient audience panel in Settings no longer breaks the page when opened.
- The empty feed can once more offer to open your own Creator profile.

- The inbox opens again. Listing conversations and opening one both failed outright.
- A locked message stays locked. Its text was being sent to the browser before it was paid for, and the inbox row quoted the opening line of it.

- Slurp no longer fails outright on an Engine that cannot hold its newer storage tables. The feed, profiles and settings work as before; messages, notifications and the audience simply stay empty until the Engine is updated.

- Messages, the audience, notifications, and the world clock work again. Slurp adds its own storage tables but never told the host about them, so each of those features failed as soon as it touched storage. On an Engine too old to accept package tables, Slurp now says so once in the log instead of erroring on every scheduler run.
